issue: BridgeElements, BridgeRiskAssessments, LoadRatingCertificates, NhvrRouteAssessments, NhvrApprovedVehicleClasses, AlertsAndNotifications, BridgeInspectionElements, BridgeCarriageways, BridgeContacts, BridgeMehComponents are exposed in AdminService with NO @restrict annotation — any authenticated user (including BMS_VIEWER with only 'view' scope) can CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE these entities via OData. The service declaration has no top-level @requires either, so CAP grants full access to any authenticated user.
fix: Add @restrict annotations to each of these entities with appropriate grants. At minimum: { grant: ['READ'], to: ['view','inspect','manage','admin'] }, { grant: ['CREATE','UPDATE'], to: ['manage','admin'] }, { grant: ['DELETE'], to: [] }. Pattern already applied correctly to BridgeInspections, BridgeDefects, BridgeConditionSurveys — replicate to all unrestricted entities.

issue: AdminService has no top-level @requires annotation. CAP falls back to 'authenticated-user' for the service root, but the entity-level @restrict annotations on unprotected entities (BridgeElements, BridgeRiskAssessments, etc.) are therefore the only gate. Without @requires on the service, any JWT bearer token (including expired tokens that pass the Bearer header check in requiresAuthentication) grants service entry. Combined with missing entity @restrict (SEC-001), the attack surface is wide open.
fix: Add @requires: ['view','inspect','manage','operate','certify','admin'] at the AdminService declaration level. This ensures CAP rejects requests with no matching scope before any entity-level check runs.

issue: The requiresAuthentication middleware accepts any request carrying 'Authorization: Bearer <anything>' as authenticated — line 1201: 'if ((req.headers.authorization || "").startsWith("Bearer ")) return next()'. This means a forged or expired JWT is accepted because the Bearer prefix is not validated. In production, BTP platform should reject forged tokens before the app, but this creates a dangerous assumption. Custom Express routes mounted before CAP's XSUAA middleware (all routes in cds.on('bootstrap')) do not have XSUAA token validation — only the Bearer prefix check. A token from another BTP subaccount or an expired token passes.
fix: Replace the bare Bearer prefix check with actual token verification using @sap/xssec verifyJwt() or xsenv + jwtMiddleware. At minimum, configure CDS to run its XSUAA middleware before the bootstrap routes, or use app.use(passport.authenticate('JWT', {session: false})) at the router level. The comment at line 1187-1193 acknowledges this weakness.

issue: requireScope middleware skips all scope checks in dummy-auth dev mode (line 1231: 'if (_isDummyAuth) return next()'). The _isDummyAuth flag is set when VCAP_SERVICES is absent AND auth.kind === 'dummy'. In CI/CD pipelines or local test environments where VCAP_SERVICES is not set but the NODE_ENV is not strictly checked, this bypass allows unrestricted access to all scope-gated endpoints. More critically, if VCAP_SERVICES is accidentally unset in a BTP deployment (e.g. misconfigured environment), all scope guards silently drop.
fix: Add a NODE_ENV !== 'production' guard: skip scope checks ONLY when NODE_ENV is explicitly 'development' or 'test', not just when VCAP_SERVICES is absent. Add a startup warning when _isDummyAuth is true. In CI, ensure VCAP_SERVICES mock is set.

issue: mountExternalApi is called with only apiLimiter — no requiresAuthentication, no requireScope (line 2791: 'mountExternalApi(app, apiLimiter)'). The external API mounts at /api/v1 and uses its own DB-backed API key check via validateApiKey(). In development mode (IS_DEV), the auth middleware in external-api.js is completely bypassed (line 284-287: 'if (IS_DEV) { res.set(...); return next() }'). In production, the only protection is an API key stored as a SystemConfig value — if SystemConfig is writable by any manage-scoped user (which it is via /system/api/config PATCH), a manage user could delete or overwrite API keys. No rate limit specific to API key abuse.
fix: Add requiresAuthentication from server.js to mountExternalApi. Move API key storage out of SystemConfig into a separate secure store (e.g. BTP Credential Store or HANA secrets). Add rate limiting per API key, not per IP only. In IS_DEV mode, still require an API key (use a hardcoded dev key).
standards: OWASP:API04 Lack of Resources & Rate Limiting

issue: AdminService still declares 'action loadDemoData()' (line 184) and 'action clearDemoData()' (line 187), both gated only by @requires: ['admin','manage']. CLAUDE.md explicitly states these were removed, but they are still declared. If the underlying demo-handler.js was deleted but the CDS declaration remains, CAP may still route these actions — or a future developer could re-add the handler without realizing these actions are in a production CDS file, reintroducing demo data loading by any manage-scoped user. Privacy Act APP11: demo data in production is a data residency and integrity violation.
fix: Remove both action declarations from admin-service.cds as stated in CLAUDE.md. Run 'npx cds compile srv/' to confirm no dangling references.

issue: CSP script-src includes both 'unsafe-inline' AND 'unsafe-eval' (line 1144). 'unsafe-eval' is required only because UI5 1.145 requireSync loader uses eval(). This disables the primary XSS protection benefit of CSP. Any DOM-based XSS gadget in the UI5 framework or application code can execute arbitrary scripts. Essential Eight Maturity Level 2 requires no unsafe-eval in CSP.
fix: Evaluate upgrading to UI5 asynchronous loading (async: true in bootstrap config) which eliminates the eval() dependency. Until then, document this deviation in the IRAP security assessment as a formal exception. Consider using SAP UI5 nonce-based CSP if the CDN supports it.

issue: The /health endpoint (line 1155) and /health/deep endpoint (line 1166) are publicly accessible with NO authentication. /health/deep returns: application version, Node.js heap usage in MB, active bridge count, and DB connectivity status. This is information disclosure that aids reconnaissance. An attacker can determine app version, infer DB state, and probe for memory exhaustion at the /health/deep endpoint (which executes a DB query on every unauthenticated request — potential DoS).
fix: Add requiresAuthentication to /health/deep. The /health probe for load balancers should return only { status: 'UP' } with no version or memory data. Move detailed health to /health/deep behind auth. Apply apiLimiter to /health/deep.

issue: The /dashboard/api router (line 1461) has requiresAuthentication but NO requireScope check. Any authenticated user — including BMS_EXTERNAL_VIEWER (who has only 'external_view' scope) — can call GET /dashboard/api/analytics which returns: total bridge count, network condition index, deficiency rate, overdue inspection details (bridgeName, state, daysOverdue), gazette expiry watchlist, scour critical count, structural sufficiency data. These are sensitive operational details not appropriate for external viewers.
fix: Add requireScope('view', 'inspect', 'manage', 'admin', 'executive_view') to the dashboardRouter mount: app.use('/dashboard/api', apiLimiter, requiresAuthentication, requireScope('view','inspect','manage','admin','executive_view'), dashboardRouter)

issue: The /map/api router (line 1626) has requiresAuthentication but NO requireScope check. GET /map/api/bridges returns lat/lon, structural details, NHVR assessment status, freight route classifications, and geoJson for all bridges. GET /map/api/export returns a full CSV/GeoJSON dump of the entire bridge network. BMS_EXTERNAL_VIEWER should only see PublicBridgeService data. Any authenticated user (including external_view scope) can download the full network GIS dataset.
fix: Add requireScope('view','inspect','manage','admin','executive_view') to /map/api mount. Alternatively create a separate /public-map/api with reduced field projection for external_view scope.
standards: Privacy Act APP11 — spatial data sensitivity

issue: The /access/api router (line 1801) has requiresAuthentication but NO requireScope — only the 'admin' or 'manage' scopes should be able to see user activity data (userId, lastSeenAt, sessionId, status, ipAddress). A BMS_VIEWER with only 'view' scope can call GET /access/api/activity and retrieve the full list of user IDs, IP addresses and session timestamps — this is PII under Privacy Act APP11.
fix: Add requireScope('admin', 'manage') to the /access/api mount.

issue: The /system/api/features GET endpoint (line 2278) is mounted with only requiresAuthentication and no apiLimiter. The PATCH /system/api/features/:key endpoint at line 2196 correctly has requireScope('config_manager','admin') but the mount at line 2278 ('app.use("/system/api/features", requiresAuthentication, featRouter)') applies only requiresAuthentication to the entire featRouter — the apiLimiter is missing. An authenticated user can spam feature flag GET requests without rate limiting.
fix: Change line 2278 to: app.use('/system/api/features', apiLimiter, requiresAuthentication, featRouter)

issue: The in-process token-bucket rate limiter (simpleRateLimit) uses req.ip as the key but does NOT account for multi-instance Cloud Foundry deployments. In BTP with 2+ app instances, each instance has its own Map — a client hitting different instances is effectively not rate-limited. The code comment at line 1420 acknowledges this: 'replace with express-rate-limit + a Redis store'. Also, _rateLimitStore grows unboundedly for unique IPs — potential memory leak in long-running instances.
fix: Replace with express-rate-limit + Redis (BTP Redis Hyperscaler Option) or use BTP API Management throttling policies. Add a periodic cleanup: setInterval(() => { const cutoff = Date.now() - windowMs; _rateLimitStore.forEach((v,k) => { if (v.start < cutoff) _rateLimitStore.delete(k) }) }, windowMs).

issue: inspectionRef auto-generation uses String.replace('INS-', '') instead of regex — seq is parseInt of potentially empty string = NaN. INS-NaN is written as inspectionRef. This is also a data integrity security concern: NaN refs appear as duplicates or null-equivalent in audit queries, allowing inspection records to evade audit trail lookups by inspectionRef.
fix: Replace line 16 with: const m = last?.inspectionRef?.match(/^INS-(\d+)$/); const seq = m ? parseInt(m[1], 10) + 1 : 1

issue: Attachment upload endpoint (POST /admin-bridges/api/bridges/:bridgeId/attachments) at line 2300 does not validate MIME type or file extension. The mediaType field is accepted from the request body as-is (line 2321: 'mediaType: mediaType || application/octet-stream'). An attacker with inspect scope can upload .html, .js, or .php files. When those files are served back via GET /admin-bridges/api/bridges/:bridgeId/attachments/:id/content at line 2337, the stored mediaType (set by the attacker) is used as Content-Type — enabling stored XSS or content sniffing attacks.
fix: (1) Add server-side MIME type validation: const ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES = new Set(['application/pdf','image/jpeg','image/png','application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document','application/vnd.ms-excel']); (2) Force Content-Disposition: attachment for all file serving; (3) Add X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff header on file responses.

issue: Attachment upload at POST /admin-bridges/api/bridges/:bridgeId/attachments has no file size validation. A user with 'inspect' scope can upload a 25MB (the express.json limit at line 2282) binary. With unlimited attachments per bridge, an attacker can exhaust HANA storage or SQLite file space. The content is stored as a binary column in BridgeDocuments — no per-bridge quota is enforced.
fix: Add base64 size check before decoding: if (contentBase64.length > 20 * 1024 * 1024 * 4/3) return 413. Add a per-bridge attachment count cap (e.g. 50) via SELECT COUNT(*) check. Consider storing attachments in BTP Object Store (S3-compatible) rather than HANA BLOB columns.

issue: /health endpoint (unauthenticated, line 1155-1164) returns process.env.npm_package_version and NODE_ENV. Exposing the exact application version enables targeted CVE exploitation. Exposing NODE_ENV='development' (if misconfigured) could reveal to an attacker that auth bypass paths are active.
fix: Remove version and env from the unauthenticated /health response. Return only { status: 'UP', ts: new Date().toISOString() }. Move version to /health/deep behind authentication.

issue: External API at /api/v1 is mounted with only apiLimiter (shared 500/15-min IP-based limiter) — no XSUAA authentication, no requiresAuthentication middleware from server.js. Protection relies solely on a DB-stored API key (X-API-Key header). The API key is stored in SystemConfig as plaintext value (category='ExternalApiKeys'). Any admin or manage user can READ SystemConfig via GET /system/api/config and see all API keys in plaintext. No key rotation mechanism, no key expiry, no key hashing.
fix: (1) Hash stored API keys with SHA-256 and compare hashes; (2) Add key metadata (expiry, label, last-used) via a dedicated ApiKeys entity; (3) Require system-level XSUAA scopes for the /api/v1 endpoint in addition to API key; (4) Apply a separate tighter rate limiter (e.g. 100/15-min) to /api/v1.

issue: execRule() in the Data Quality rules engine accesses bridge[field] where 'field' comes from DB-stored DataQualityRules.field (line 1868). The ALLOWED_RULE_FIELDS allowlist (line 2051) is only enforced on POST/PUT /quality/api/rules. An admin who directly UPDATEs the DataQualityRules table (via OData AdminService.DataQualityRules which has no @restrict) can set field='__proto__' or field='constructor' — enabling prototype pollution when bridge[field] is read during rule evaluation.
fix: (1) Add @restrict to AdminService.DataQualityRules entity (currently has none); (2) In execRule(), validate field against ALLOWED_RULE_FIELDS before the bridge[field] access: 'if (!ALLOWED_RULE_FIELDS.has(ruleType === "required_field" || ruleType === "non_zero" ? field : "")) return false'

issue: BNAC environment baseUrl is accepted from user input and stored without URL validation (line 2684: 'patch.baseUrl = baseUrl.endsWith("/") ? baseUrl : baseUrl + "/"'). The baseUrl is later used to construct bnacUrl for each bridge mapping (line 2757: 'const bnacUrl = baseUrl ? baseUrl + bnacObjectId : ""'). If an attacker with admin scope sets baseUrl to 'javascript://' or 'file:///', the constructed bnacUrl values are stored in BnacObjectIdMap and later rendered as clickable links in the UI (DataFieldWithUrl annotation in fiori-service.cds) — enabling stored XSS / JavaScript injection via bnacUrl.
fix: Validate baseUrl with: if (!/^https:\/\//.test(baseUrl)) return res.status(400).json({ error: { message: 'baseUrl must start with https://' } }) before storing.

issue: loadClusters() uses raw SQL string interpolation for cellSize (lines 928-984). Although cellSize is computed server-side from zoomToCellSize() and is always a numeric literal (0.1, 0.25, etc.), the pattern sets a dangerous precedent: the comment on line 921 says 'cellSize is a server-computed number (not user input) — safe to interpolate'. However, the zoom parameter IS user-controlled (line 1572: 'zoom: req.query.zoom') and is passed to loadClusters as Number(zoom). If zoomToCellSize returns null (zoom > 8), the fallback loadMapBridges branch is taken. If a future developer adds new zoom values, cellSize could become user-controlled. Additionally, 'postingStatus' string literals are hardcoded in the raw SQL — these are not parameterised.
fix: Use db.run(cds.ql.SELECT...) for clustering wherever possible instead of raw SQL strings. If raw SQL is unavoidable, assert that cellSize is one of the pre-defined values: const VALID_CELL_SIZES = new Set([2.0, 1.0, 0.5, 0.25, 0.1]); if (!VALID_CELL_SIZES.has(cellSize)) throw new Error('Invalid cell size').

issue: /quality/api is mounted with requiresAuthentication and validateCsrfToken but NO requireScope (line 2120). POST /quality/api/rules, PUT /quality/api/rules/:id, and DELETE /quality/api/rules/:id are writable by any authenticated user including BMS_VIEWER (view scope only). Data quality rules drive completeness scoring and can be used to suppress visibility of genuine data deficiencies — a malicious user with view scope could delete all critical rules.
fix: Add requireScope('admin', 'manage') to the /quality/api mount, or add it per-route to POST, PUT, DELETE within qualityRouter.

issue: GET /mass-upload/api/register accepts 'limit' and 'offset' as query parameters (line 1371) with parseInt but no numeric cap on offset. An extreme offset value could cause the XLSX.utils.sheet_to_json iteration to process the entire exported CSV before slicing — potential CPU exhaustion on large datasets. There is also no cap on 'limit' other than the parseInt fallback.
fix: Add: const start = Math.max(0, Math.min(parseInt(offset,10)||0, 10000)); const end = start + Math.min(parseInt(limit,10)||200, 500);

issue: mountReportsApi is called at line 2789: 'mountReportsApi(app, requiresAuthentication)'. Based on recon.json, this mounts reports endpoints. If the reports API does not apply requireScope (only requiresAuthentication is passed), report endpoints returning risk registers, defect data, and structural assessments are accessible to BMS_EXTERNAL_VIEWER. The recon gap list confirms reports-api.js queries bridge.management.Bridges directly.
fix: Pass requireScope into mountReportsApi and apply requireScope('view','inspect','manage','admin','executive_view') to all report endpoints. Audit reports-api.js for missing scope guards.

issue: The QR/PDF API is mounted at line 2644 as a second app.use on /admin-bridges/api WITHOUT the validateCsrfToken middleware that the first mount (line 2641) has. Any POST/DELETE endpoints in qrApi do not get CSRF protection. The comment shows the mount was added separately from the main adminBridgeRouter.
fix: Consolidate all /admin-bridges/api routes into a single mount with consistent middleware, or add validateCsrfToken explicitly to qrApi: app.use('/admin-bridges/api', requiresAuthentication, validateCsrfToken, qrApi)

issue: The request logger (lines 1098-1120) logs req.user.id on every request (line 1109: 'userId: req.user?.id || ... || "anonymous"'). This includes all OData and REST paths. For paths that include PII parameters (e.g. GET /odata/v4/admin/Bridges?$filter=bridgeName eq 'John Smith Bridge') the full path is logged. The log entry is written to stdout with console.log which in BTP goes to Application Logging Service — logs may not have appropriate access controls or retention limits.
fix: Scrub PII from logged paths: replace path logging with only the base path (req.path.split('?')[0]). Ensure Application Logging Service in mta.yaml has log retention set to <= 90 days per Privacy Act APP11 data minimisation. Do not log query string parameters.

issue: AdminService exposes UserActivity as @readonly projection with no @restrict annotation. GET /odata/v4/admin/UserActivity returns userId, lastSeenAt, sessionId, status, ipAddress for all users. This is PII under Privacy Act APP11. Any authenticated user (even BMS_VIEWER) can query this OData endpoint to enumerate all active sessions and IP addresses.
fix: Add @restrict: [{ grant: ['READ'], to: ['admin','manage'] }] to the UserActivity projection in admin-service.cds.

issue: AdminService exposes SystemConfig as a full projection with no @restrict annotation (line 151: 'entity SystemConfig as projection on my.SystemConfig'). GET /odata/v4/admin/SystemConfig returns all config keys and values including ExternalApiKeys values (plaintext API keys), appMaintenanceMode, feature flags, and any other sensitive configuration. Any authenticated user can read these.
fix: Add @restrict: [{ grant: ['READ'], to: ['admin','manage','config_manager'] }, { grant: ['CREATE','UPDATE','DELETE'], to: ['admin','config_manager'] }] to SystemConfig in admin-service.cds. This is separate from the /system/api REST endpoint which correctly applies requireScope('admin').

issue: IS_DEV flag at line 5 is determined by absence of VCAP_SERVICES. In CI/CD pipelines, integration tests, and container environments, VCAP_SERVICES may not be set even in non-local environments. When IS_DEV=true, the external API auth middleware at line 284 completely skips API key validation and sets an X-BMS-Warning header instead. This means in any CI/CD test job or misconfigured container, the External API serves full bridge data without authentication.
fix: Use NODE_ENV strictly: const IS_DEV = process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development'. Never rely on absence of VCAP_SERVICES as the dev mode signal.

issue: BridgeContacts entity (from gap-entities.cds) contains contact person PII: primaryContact (name), organisation, position, phone, mobile, address, email. This entity has no @restrict annotation in AdminService (line 73 admin-service.cds: 'entity BridgeContacts as projection on my.BridgeContacts' — no @restrict). Also no audit log coverage (writeChangeLogs not called in any handler for BridgeContacts per recon.json). PII mutations are untracked.
fix: (1) Add @restrict to BridgeContacts in admin-service.cds; (2) Ensure bridge contacts CRUD goes through a handler that calls writeChangeLogs(); (3) Add @PersonalData.FieldSemantics annotations for Privacy Act compliance in the CDS model.

issue: recon.json 'missing_resources' notes: 'connectivity service — external-api.js makes outbound calls but no BTP connectivity service is declared in mta.yaml'. The external-api.js module (specifically validateApiKey and any outbound bridge data calls) runs in Cloud Foundry without a declared Connectivity service binding. Outbound HTTP calls without Connectivity service bypass BTP's egress proxy and network policy controls, making it impossible to audit or restrict outbound connections from the app.
fix: Add BridgeManagement-connectivity (connectivity) as an mta.yaml resource and bind it to the srv module. Use the BTP Destination service for all external HTTP calls rather than direct fetch().

issue: xs-security.json uses tenant-mode: 'dedicated' (line 4). This correctly restricts the app to a single BTP subaccount tenant. However, the attributes array is empty (line 16: 'attributes: []'). Without XSUAA attributes, it is impossible to implement row-level or state-level data isolation via XSUAA — e.g. restricting BMS_OPERATOR to NSW bridges only. The operate scope description says 'Manage restrictions in assigned state' but no XSUAA attribute enforces the state assignment. State filtering is purely application-level (no DB-level restriction).
fix: Define a 'state' attribute in xs-security.json: { 'name': 'state', 'description': 'Assigned Australian state for operators', 'valueType': 'string' }. Then reference it in role-templates for BMS_OPERATOR. In the CAP service, add @restrict: [{ grant: ['CREATE','UPDATE'], to: 'operate', where: 'state = $user.state' }] on Restrictions.

issue: BridgeContacts ipAddress and sessionId fields in UserActivity are stored persistently and returned in /access/api/activity. Storing IP addresses in HANA without a defined retention policy may violate Privacy Act APP11 (data minimisation). There is no TTL or automatic expiry on UserActivity records.
fix: Add a scheduled cleanup job (BTP Job Scheduling service) to delete UserActivity records older than 90 days. Or add a lastSeenAt-based WHERE clause in recordActivity() to only retain the last N days. Document the retention period in the privacy impact assessment.

issue: buildBridgeCardHtml generates an HTML page with 'window.onload = function() { window.print(); }' (line 2509) and is served with Content-Type: text/html. The bridge card endpoint at GET /admin-bridges/api/bridges/:bridgeId/card is behind auth but returns an HTML page that auto-triggers window.print(). While the HTML uses esc() for all user data, the Content-Disposition is not set to 'attachment' — the HTML is rendered directly in the browser. If any future change misses an esc() call on a new field, XSS is possible in an authenticated context.
fix: Add 'Content-Security-Policy: default-src none; style-src unsafe-inline; script-src unsafe-inline' header specifically on the card response to scope CSP to just that page. Consider adding X-Frame-Options: DENY to prevent clickjacking.

issue: ChangeLog entity is marked @readonly in admin-service.cds (line 141). However, ChangeLog has no @restrict annotation — any authenticated user can read the full audit trail via OData: GET /odata/v4/admin/ChangeLog. Audit logs contain changedBy (user IDs), objectId, fieldName, oldValue, newValue for all entity mutations including sensitive field changes (e.g. condition ratings, permitRef approvals). This is a PII and information disclosure concern.
fix: Add @restrict: [{ grant: ['READ'], to: ['admin','manage'] }] to the ChangeLog projection. Alternatively keep the @readonly and add the restrict. The /audit/api REST endpoint correctly requires admin/manage scope — the OData endpoint should match.

issue: BNAC CSV upload at POST /bnac/api/upload (line 2721) decodes the CSV and parses rows. There is no validation on the number of rows — an admin could upload a CSV with millions of rows causing an in-process loop over all lines (line 2748: 'for (const line of dataLines)'). Each iteration does two DB calls (SELECT one + INSERT/UPDATE). This is a CPU/DB exhaustion DoS vector for any user with admin scope.
fix: Add: if (dataLines.length > 10000) return res.status(400).json({ error: { message: 'CSV too large: max 10,000 rows per upload' } })
